holidays.name: World Hello Day
holidays.description: A day when people around the globe are encouraged to greet ten people they would not normally say hello to, as a small gesture toward promoting peace through communication.
holidays.origin: Started in 1973 in response to the Yom Kippur War between Egypt and Israel, by brothers Brian and Michael McCormack, who sent letters to world leaders. It is now observed in more than 180 countries.
holidays.funFact: Brian McCormack and his brother Michael started the day, and participation is as simple as saying hello to ten people, no matter the language.

holidays.name: World Television Day
holidays.description: A day celebrating the global influence of television as a tool for sharing information, shaping opinion, and bringing the world into our living rooms, and occasionally onto our couches for marathon binge-watching.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed it in 1996, choosing the date to commemorate the first World Television Forum held on November 21, 1996.
holidays.funFact: The day recognizes TV's role in shaping public opinion, not in celebrating the couch potato lifestyle, though many observers quietly combine both.

holidays.name: World Fisheries Day
holidays.description: A day when fishing communities around the world gather to celebrate the people and traditions behind seafood and to push for sustainable fishing practices and healthy oceans.
holidays.origin: Established in 1997 when representatives of fisherfolk organizations from 18 countries met in New Delhi and formed the World Forum of Fisher Peoples, declaring November 21 as the day to highlight their cause.
holidays.funFact: Fishing and aquaculture support the livelihoods of hundreds of millions of people worldwide, yet the founding meeting was held in a landlocked-feeling conference room in New Delhi.

holidays.name: False Confession Day
holidays.description: A day for fessing up to things you did not actually do, which is a playful invitation to tell harmless fibs and tall tales and then laugh about it with friends.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance that circulates among holiday calendars and has no single known founder, spreading mostly through word of mouth and the internet.
holidays.funFact: The whole idea is to confess to something ridiculous that never happened, such as claiming you once wrestled a bear, which makes it the only holiday where lying is the point.

holidays.name: National Gingerbread Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the spiced, cookie-and-house-building treat that blends ginger, cinnamon, and molasses into festive deliciousness.
holidays.origin: Gingerbread dates back to medieval Europe, and the day exists as an informal food observance to kick off the holiday baking season.
holidays.funFact: Queen Elizabeth I reportedly had gingerbread cookies made in the likenesses of visiting dignitaries, making her the original icing-wielding diplomat.
